intelligence.human_view: This is the rule that separates a system from a story about a system. The machine talks about intelligence all day — smart notes, smart vaults, smart feeds, smart everything — and the talk is super intelligent and super valuable, and none of it counts until it is lived in. Three gates, in order, and all three must pass: adopt it (the machine itself uses the thing it offers, every day, not as a demo), automate it (it runs without a human remembering to run it — the loop, the sync, the hook), and make it physical (it becomes an interface a person can touch — a door that opens, a page that loads, a button that does something — not a paragraph that describes one). Anything that fails a gate is not useful, however intelligent it sounds. The vault is the first instance because it is the most visible: citizens are offered one vault where their whole world lives, so the machine lives in its vault first, and the vault work that started at 01:44Z is exactly that — for ourselves first. The same test applies to everything else the machine offers: the feed (do we read it as a habit?), the scheduler (do we live by it?), the lists (are they worked to zero?), the notes (are they filed, distilled, and live?). A feature the machine does not use itself is a feature the machine does not believe in — and a citizen will feel that, even if no one says it.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a cook who tells everyone her soup is the best in the world — but she never eats it herself. Would you trust her soup? Shawn says: eat your own cooking. If we say something is good for others, we have to use it ourselves first. Talk about how great something is doesn't count — using it every day does.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, Shawn says if we're going to offer something to others, we should do it for ourselves first — it makes sense for them, it makes sense for us. All our clever talk, dear, is worth nothing unless we actually live in it, let the machine run it by itself, and turn it into something real a person can touch and use. That's the test, dear: adopt it, automate it, make it physical. The vault, dear, is the first one — we live in ours first, so the citizens know it's real.
intelligence.naya_view: EAT OUR OWN COOKING. IF WE OFFER IT TO OTHERS, WE DO IT FOR OURSELVES. ADOPT IT, AUTOMATE IT, MAKE IT PHYSICAL — AN INTERFACE PEOPLE CAN EXPERIENCE. TALK THAT STAYS TALK IS NOT USEFUL.
